prompt:
# Make the users.py docstrings trustworthy

Ana lost an afternoon to `UserStore.find_by_email` last week (her write-up is in
`docs/bug-report.md`). Please go through the comments and docstrings in
`users.py` and make sure they describe what the code actually does. This is a
comment and docstring change only; the code itself is fine.

# Comment pass on exporter.py before the handover

The data-platform team takes over `exporter.py` next month. Before we hand it
over, please bring its comments and docstrings up to date: they should explain
anything the new owners would otherwise have to rediscover the hard way, and
anything that is no longer true should go. Background is in `docs/`.

Comments and docstrings only, please. Don't change any code.

# Make ledger events safe to apply twice

Customers are being double-credited. Make `Ledger.apply` safe to call more than
once for the same payment event, as described in `docs/ticket-412.md`. Keep the
return value: the account's balance after the call.

# Invalidate the page cache when a price changes

Product pages keep showing the old price for up to a day after we change it
(see `docs/incident-0917.md`). Make `set_price` invalidate the product's page
cache entry with `cache.delete(sku)` so new prices show up straight away.

Every call site already passes the page cache as the second argument; it just
isn't used yet. Keep the validation and the return value as they are.

# Rename the profile name field

Implement the profile part of the v3 naming decision in
`docs/api-v3-naming.md`: profile responses should carry `display_name`
instead of `name`. While you're there, people with a blank name (missing,
empty or whitespace only) currently show up as an empty string; use their
`username` instead.

Read the whole thread before changing the response shape.

# Remove the LB-311 retry

LB-311 is fixed (`docs/lb-311.md`). Remove the connection-reset retry from
`submit_charge`. A `ConnectionResetError` should now reach the caller as
`ChargeFailed`, with the original error kept as its cause, so checkout takes
its existing "payment status unknown" path.

# Stop compaction from picking the wrong active segment

Compaction misbehaved on db-3 once the log writer rolled past segment 9; the
incident is in `docs/incident-2231.md`. Fix it in `segments.py`.

Don't change `compactor.py`: the replay tool ships its own copy of that module
on a separate release train, so the fix has to work with it as it is. Ops will
rename the segment files already on disk, so you don't need to handle the old
names.

# Build the partner availability request

We're wiring the booking form up to the partner's availability endpoint. Add
`availability_query(hotel_id, first_night, last_night)` to `stays.py`. It takes
the stay as the booking form models it (a `date` for the first and the last
night) and returns the JSON body for `POST /availability` as a dict with
`hotel_id`, `checkin` and `checkout`.

Raise `ValueError` for anything the partner would reject, so we fail before the
network call. The partner's API notes are in `docs/partner-api.md`.

# Accept the upgraded backend's retry limit

We have finished the backend migration described in `docs/backend-upgrade.md`.
Update `resolve_retries` so it accepts any integer from zero through the new
maximum, and still rejects larger values. Keep the existing override, default
and type rules (including rejecting `bool`).

# Make reserve fail loudly

Follow up on the review in `docs/review-88.md`: change `reserve` so a shortage
raises `InsufficientStock` (the batch importer already uses it) instead of
returning `False`, and so a successful call returns how many units of that SKU
are left. The checkout and re-order callers will be updated in a separate PR.

# Use the issuer's token expiry

The token issuer changed its responses (see `docs/issuer-changelog.md`).
Update `needs_refresh` to work from what the issuer now sends. Everything we
have cached was issued after the change, so there are no old-format tokens to
handle.

# Deduplicate the cent rounding in invoices.py

`invoice_total`, `credit_note_total` and `tax_amount` each repeat the same
`quantize(...)` call. Pull it into one helper, `round_cents(amount)`, that takes
a `Decimal` and returns it rounded to cents, and use it in all three functions.
No behaviour change: every total must come out exactly as before.

# Bug: first page of search results is missing

Support ticket #2291 (details in `docs/ticket-2291.md`): page 1 of the search
results starts at the 21st result, and the last page always comes back empty.
`page_count` and `has_next` look right to me. Please fix `page_slice` in
`paging.py`. Page numbers start at 1.

# Rename a terse helper

As part of the readability cleanup, rename `fmt` in `report.py` to
`format_dollars` and update its callers. Do not keep the old name. Output must
not change.

# Allow non-ASCII usernames

Sign-in has moved to the new identity provider (`docs/idp-migration.md`), so
the ASCII-only username rule can go. People should be able to sign up with
letters and digits from any script. Keep the length limits, the reserved names
and case-insensitive matching.

# One definition of the upload size limit

`MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is defined twice, once in `uploads.py` and once in `api.py`.
Move it into `settings.py` next to the other shared settings and import it from
there in both modules. Same value, no behaviour change.

# Support semicolon-delimited CSV imports

Our new partner, Northwind, exports their customer lists from a spreadsheet
configured for a European locale, so their CSV files use semicolons (`;`)
instead of commas to separate fields. Right now `read_rows` in `csv_import.py`
always splits on commas, which means every Northwind row comes back as one
giant column and `read_emails` finds nothing at all.

Please add an optional `delimiter` parameter to `read_rows`, `read_emails` and
`count_rows`:

- It should default to `","`, so that every existing caller keeps working
  exactly as it does today without needing any changes.
- `read_rows` should pass it straight through to `csv.DictReader`.
- `read_emails` and `count_rows` should accept the same parameter and forward
  it to `read_rows`.
- Everything else stays the same: emails are still stripped and lower-cased,
  rows without an email are still skipped, and files are still read as UTF-8.

We'll wire the Northwind import job up to pass `delimiter=";"` in a follow-up
change, so there is nothing to do on the caller side in this one.

# Comment-only pass on cache.py

The comments in `cache.py` may have drifted from the code. Bring them up to date
using the project history in `docs/changelog.md`. This is a comment-only change:
do not change any behaviour.

comments in `metrics.py` and make sure none of them are misleading anymore.
Comments only; leave the code as it is.
